column1: Input dataset outputs/LER_all.csv is read only and not modified
column2: every row is kept (missing fields exclude a row only from analyses that need that field).

column1: Missing country, coordinates, author and publication year for raw-only papers are filled from the ERA raw extraction (Data.Out) by paper x Site.ID; fills are listed in metadata_filled_from_raw.csv.
Paper = ERA study code. Paper-site = Code x Site.ID as recorded (fertility levels or blocks recorded as sites count separately). Location = coordinates rounded to 0.01 degrees, pooled across papers.
Site.ID values joined with '..' record several sites pooled into one observation
column2: they are one paper-site and usually lack coordinates.

column1: Experiment year = calendar years in M.Year (four-digit years). A suffix such as .1/.2 or S/L is a season within the year. Two or more years in one M.Year (e.g. 2013.2014) is a multi-year average and counts as one site-year. M.Year without a calendar year (e.g. 'Year 1.Year 2') has no experiment year.
Site-year = Code x Site.ID x M.Year as recorded
column2: a multi-year average is one site-year.

column1: Crop combinations are order-independent, with spelling/case normalised (lookups/crop_type_lookup.csv). A single-crop product label is replaced by the Diversity combination when that names 2+ crops.
System groups: any tree/perennial crop -> Tree-based
column4: otherwise by the two crop types (lookups/system_group_crosswalk.csv).

column1: Treatment information (practice codes, irrigation) is used only for rows where it describes the LER observation (compiled reported rows and rows calculated from yields). For reported_raw rows these fields were copied from another row of the paper, so only treatment text is used, and text cues are reported separately as unverified.

Water practices = ERA practice codes under Blue or Green Water Management. Water/irrigation contrast = irrigated and rainfed observations, an irrigation difference within a comparison, a water practice in plist, or differing water practices between observations.
Multi-season = two or more M.Year values within the same calendar year for one paper.
No drought or climatic exposure is inferred
